newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian consortium bids to build Ashland vessel.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian consortium bids to build Ashland vessel.

text.p: A consortium of two Nigerian firms is bidding to construct a floating and production storage facility for Ashland Oil Company, a company official said on Wednesday.
The firms are Nigerdock and the National Engineering and Technical Company (NETCO), a joint-venture between state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation and Bechtel of USA.

"We are bidding for the design, procurement, modification and construction of a tanker vessel for a floating storage and off-loading (FPSO) facility for Ashland Oil," Alex Ogedegbe, managing director of NETCO, told Reuters.
Ogedegbe said NETCO and Nigerdock had signed a memorandum of understanding to form a consortium to bid for oil industry contracts.
The Nigerian government said in October that contracts in the petroleum sector, the country's economic backbone, would only be awarded to firms registered in the country.
Ogedegbe said NETCO would undertake engineering services for Mobil Corp's Nigerian production unit beginning next year.
"This involves designs for new pipelines, civil and process engineering, to meet Mobil's expansion programmes," he said.
